claims.statement: The delivery projection maps each Context to exactly one DeliveryService whose id is `service.<contextRef without the `context.` prefix>` and whose lane is the last dotted segment of the Context id; services are sorted by Context id and links by link id, so two runs of the projector name the same boundaries.

A service's kind is decided by capability first and Context kind second: a Context that answers another Context's evidence-kind socket is `capability`, otherwise `pre_contract` becomes `channel`, `domain` becomes `domain`, and every remaining Context becomes `fulfillment`.

Capability sockets are never declared twice: a `plays_role` relationship whose target is a `role` of kind `evidence` in a different Context makes the player's Context the supplier, filling `supplies` on the supplier, `consumes` on the consumer, and emitting a `link.capability.*` link with `mode: 'async'` because the confirmation arrives from the supplier's own clock as a callback.

`reads` links (sync) are derived from rule bindings that reference a Domain Context and from `references` relationships reaching into one, while a `signs` link (sync) runs from a `pre_contract` Context to its `parentContextRef`, labelled with that Context's root contract.

`buildDeliveryDeployment` renders one compose service per Context with `EVIDENCE_MODEL`, `EVIDENCE_CONTEXT`, `EVIDENCE_SERVICE_KIND` and `EVIDENCE_BASE_PATH`, `dependsOn` taken exactly from the links leaving that service and `expose` from the route lanes it serves; images and ports are placeholders, so the file is a sketch rather than a release.

Each fulfillment pair yields a `POST` request route, a `GET` ledger route and one `POST` confirm route per confirmation, with 201 and 409 on request, 200 and 404 on ledger and 201, 409 and 422 on confirm; a contract Context's root contract additionally gets a `POST` sign route (201, 422) and a `GET` read route (200, 404).

A pre-contract Context yields `open` and `read` routes per enquiry plus a `propose` route per proposal, nested under the enquiry only when a `references` relationship ties them and otherwise left at the lane root; a Domain Context yields only `GET` read routes for its `participant`/`thing` objects, because a domain answer is read and never written by a caller.

Addressing is derived rather than assigned: `rawSegmentOf` folds the last dotted id part into a path word, `createSegmentAllocator` disambiguates only clashes inside one id category with `-<category>` and then `-<category>-<n>` suffixes, and `operationIdFor` builds the camel-cased operation id from verb plus id.

A route's `shape` and `itemPath` come from `childShape`, which reads the `references` cardinality at whichever endpoint holds the child regardless of arrow direction and answers `singleton` only when every maximum found is 1; the final pass rewrites `/requests` to `/request`, adds `{requestId}` or `{confirmationId}` only for collection shapes, and appends a confirmation segment when a request has more than one confirmation.

`callerRoles` narrows the root contract's `roleRefs` by the evidence's `responsibleRoleRef` and then keeps only `role`/`party` entities that a `participant`/`party` actually plays through `plays_role`; an empty result makes the route `exposure: 'internal'` while keeping it in the snapshot, the OpenAPI paths and the topology.

`fieldFor` classifies an attribute as `derived` when a derivation rule resolves or `derivedByRuleRef` is set, otherwise `service-time` when its name is one of the five business clock attributes (`started_at`, `expired_at`, `signed_at`, `confirmed_at`, `created_at`), otherwise `caller`; a dangling `derivedByRuleRef` still classifies as derived, so a missing rule never silently turns a value into caller input.

The OpenAPI request body contains only `caller`-classified fields with `additionalProperties: false`, while server-owned values appear only in component schemas marked `readOnly` with `x-evidence-origin`, `x-evidence-caller-input: false` and the rule reference; a stamped business time such as `confirmed_at` is therefore absent from the writable type and cannot be supplied or backdated by a caller.

`deliveryFilesOf` writes `openapi.json`, `topology.json`, `routes.json`, `deployment.compose.json`, `projection.json`, `http-journeys.json` (with `runtimeValidated: false`) and `limitations.md` only when limitations exist; limitations report unconfirmed fulfillment requests and derived attributes that need a server-side rule runtime.

`diffModelToApi` projects both documents with their optional design overlays and compares the finished snapshots through `diffApiSnapshots`, which refuses different `modelId` values with `API_MODEL_MISMATCH`; the returned result also carries `modelChanges` from `diffDomainModels`, so a reader can join model movement to interface movement.

Routes are matched by `route.id` and navigation links by source route, rel and target, and both sides are normalized before comparison by sorting fields, derived, stamped, outputFields, party roles, responses and rules — so a renamed path on a known route is `PATH_CHANGED` and reordering declarations in the model produces no diff at all.

Breaking findings about route identity and address are `ROUTE_REMOVED` (the route id is gone, reported alone and immediately), `PATH_CHANGED` (path or itemPath differs), `METHOD_CHANGED`, `OPERATION_ID_CHANGED`, `CALLER_ROLE_RESTRICTED` (a previously allowed party role dropped) and `STATUS_CODE_CHANGED` (the 2xx status set differs).

Payload and semantic breaking findings are `REQUIRED_FIELD_ADDED`, `INPUT_FIELD_REMOVED`, `FIELD_REMOVED_FROM_RESPONSE`, `FIELD_TYPE_CHANGED`, `RESPONSE_FIELD_OPTIONAL`, `RULE_CHANGED` (a bound rule changed, or a non-derivation rule was added) and `NAVIGATION_LINK_REMOVED` (a non-self link on a surviving route disappeared).

Field diffs are keyed by attribute name over `outputFields` and add `shifted: 'to_derived'` or `'to_caller'` when the origin changed plus `requiredChanged` when only the mandatory flag moved; a caller-to-derived shift therefore also raises `INPUT_FIELD_REMOVED`.

`renderApiDiff` emits a text report with added/removed/modified markers, `[BREAKING]` tags, field diffs, findings and both sides' diagnostics, ending with `No API changes.` when nothing moved; the CLI `diff` verb exits 0 when the revisions agree, 3 when there are breaking changes or gaps, and 1 for load failures or `API_MODEL_MISMATCH`, and it refuses `--out` so a comparison cannot overwrite anything.

`patchDeliveryRoutes` first validates that the model diff describes exactly the target document's entities, relationships and rules, then widens the affected Context set through global segment reallocation, changed role players and pre-contract parent inheritance, rebuilds only those Contexts with `buildDeliveryRoutes`, reuses byte-identical route objects and preserves untouched routes; tests require the patched list to equal a full rebuild in both directions.

The live delivery preview is computed in the main process from the renderer's in-memory document plus its editor-open baseline with no disk read, and returns the snapshot's model digest, route bindings, the rendered change log, the API coverage summary, the issues, and `canExportDraft` true only when no issue has severity `block`.

`exportLiveDelivery` clones the input before opening the asynchronous directory picker, recomputes the analysis from that frozen clone, refuses a preview whose digest no longer equals `expectedModelDigest` and refuses blocking issues, then writes the normal delivery tree plus `api-changes.md` and `draft-status.json` carrying `mode: 'draft'`, `releaseAuthorized: false` and both digests.

The saved-project path previews and exports by re-projecting the sources on disk through `readDelivery`, which refuses a model with errors, writes only `deliveryFilesOf` output, and suggests `<project>/delivery`; unlike the live path it carries no digest handshake, so a model saved between preview and export is exported as it now stands on disk.

One `useDeliveryHub` subscription debounces document changes by 150 ms, drops replies from superseded revisions, keeps the editor-open document as the baseline across undo, redo and save, marks the preview stale and blocks export while recomputing, and exports only the accepted preview together with its model digest.

The delivery hub renders two tabs: a full contract view of services with route counts and kind notes, crossings with sync or async mode, route bindings with exposure or allowed party roles and the limitations; and an incremental diff view with both digests, route change counts, API coverage and non-`API_ALIGNED` issues, a copyable Markdown change log, and a warning that breaking changes leave release unauthorized.

In draft mode the API sensor maps a snapshot diagnostic of severity `error` to `block` and a breaking change to `warn`, so an interface break is flagged but still exportable as a draft, while `mode: 'release'` turns the same break into a blocking finding.

The live preview's route bindings also feed the canvas `LiveApiProvider` for route badges, and the MCP tools `get_delivery_topology` and `export_openapi_contract` answer the same question for external agents from the saved sources through `readDelivery`, per-service route counts included.
